Doc,

I see what Maknil means in his charts, thanks for highlighting this Maknil

. Can I

just clear my way of thinking to see if it correct with the ways Pro money trade?

If I see a key level on the Daily that has seen a break with force indicating professional money is in play, I would then first check to see if there is a reasonable target on the Daily, presuming we get a pullback to the key level that has just seen the break.

I would then check the 4hr to see if P.A is any clearer for another possible target, more near term, or where price may run into difficulty which is not clear on the daily.

I would then set up my monitor to have a 15 min/30min and an hourly timeframe (these are the timeframes I feel most comfortable with entering for the time being). and then wait for price to retrace near my key level box and watch LTF P.A in all of these 3 timeframes.

I have done a little live trading, only with 0.10 lots. But my main testing comes from using the Forex tester where I have been able to log and print every trade I do, this seems to have helped me a lot with screen time education as I know you recommend.

If the above description is not clear the way I wrote it, I can pst up some charts to show. Thanks for your time Doc, much appreciated.

What should jump out at you after marking off historic supply and demand areas is that eventually all the boxes in their respective time frames will overlap. If you wait for this to happen the probability of a winning trade is much greater.

Hotochin's comment about price getting closer is one time when this way of trading is not going to give large results, you must look for room for profit and when price gets squeezed on higher time frames pro money wont leave orders in there keeping capital tied up. Price must move between supply and demand and when any factor effects the movement over a reasonable period of time, expect a squeeze to happen and plenty chop. It is better to look for other pairs than guessing when the break will happen.

Fortunately we do have a way to deal with this, its called patience and discipline and wait for the break, then the pull back and restest of the break to see will it hold and is there excess orders waiting for a continuation. Price action at those time and at those areas is key. The old traders often mention time and price, but its meaning is lost on most traders today.

Master marking off areas and then look for price action, just get one working first and then work on the other. You are slowing getting there Hotochin, stick to it and it gets easier.

Hotochin,

Waiting for price to hit supply or demand on the monthly and weekly is not something you or I can afford. But we must be aware than when it does hit these areas there is going to be a reaction and a likely change in direction. Once the new direction has been decided by pro money, we now drop down into daily and lower time frames to look for pull backs counter to the decided direction and look for those pull backs to be the restest of the origin of the move. The retest appears deeper on lower time frames whereas the daily generally will not pull back very much.

If you think about it logically, any low time frame within a day traders pocket is ripe for false moves and stop hunts. This is how most of the larger orders get filled. When you see the price turn against a break of even a few hours, think of this as the test of the strength of the bulls or bears. If they want to continue with the move they will close some of the positions because you are now taking the orders as the market is moving. The false sense of security plays out on all low time frames and all it does is hand a very low cost and low risk entry for pro money to reverse price back on the direction of the chosen direction.

When price is between lets say the 4hr or higher time frame supply and demand, my choice is only take a trade once a pull back has come and it is into an area where pro money was active. If the move fails my risk is small. Ideally you should not take a trade when mid range between supply and demand and take the easy trades, the type you can see from across the room!

As you get more screen under your belt you will see how price wants to come back to the origin of the move. It will give you one and sometimes a second shot at getting in. There are a few gotchas in day trading and what can mess up nice entries just waiting to be taken are the release of news and the time of day. When London in particular opens and closes price will not always react as you expect if it is approaching an area of historic price action and its best to stand aside and wait for the market to settle.

It boils down to lining up time frames and historic price action with current price action. However, it takes a long time to get your brain to work against what it sees on the hard right edge of the screen. Books tell you wait for confirmation, I say active pro money is confirmation, and pro money is its own confirmation.

صبر کردن برای اینکه قیمت به عرضه یا تقاضای ماهانه و هفتگی برسد، چیزی نیست که تو یا من از عهده‌اش بربیاییم. اما باید بدانیم وقتی به این نواحی می‌رسد، واکنشی در کار است و احتمالاً تغییر جهت. وقتی پول حرفه‌ای جهت جدید را مشخص کرد، تازه می‌آییم پایین، به روزانه و تایم‌فریم‌های پایین‌تر، تا پولبک‌های خلاف جهتِ تعیین‌شده را پیدا کنیم و ببینیم آن پولبک‌ها همان ریتست مبدأ حرکت هستند. ریتست در تایم‌فریم‌های پایین‌تر عمیق‌تر دیده می‌شود، در حالی که روزانه معمولاً پولبک زیادی نمی‌زند.

Doctor wrote: Hotochin,

Waiting for price to hit supply or demand on the monthly and weekly is not something you or I can afford. But we must be aware than when it does hit these areas there is going to be a reaction and a likely change in direction. Once the new direction has been decided by pro money, we now drop down into daily and lower time frames to look for pull backs counter to the decided direction and look for those pull backs to be the restest of the origin of the move. The retest appears deeper on lower time frames whereas the daily generally will not pull back very much.

If you think about it logically, any low time frame within a day traders pocket is ripe for false moves and stop hunts. This is how most of the larger orders get filled. When you see the price turn against a break of even a few hours, think of this as the test of the strength of the bulls or bears. If they want to continue with the move they will close some of the positions because you are now taking the orders as the market is moving. The false sense of security plays out on all low time frames and all it does is hand a very low cost and low risk entry for pro money to reverse price back on the direction of the chosen direction.

When price is between lets say the 4hr or higher time frame supply and demand, my choice is only take a trade once a pull back has come and it is into an area where pro money was active. If the move fails my risk is small. Ideally you should not take a trade when mid range between supply and demand and take the easy trades, the type you can see from across the room!

As you get more screen under your belt you will see how price wants to come back to the origin of the move. It will give you one and sometimes a second shot at getting in. There are a few gotchas in day trading and what can mess up nice entries just waiting to be taken are the release of news and the time of day. When London in particular opens and closes price will not always react as you expect if it is approaching an area of historic price action and its best to stand aside and wait for the market to settle.

It boils down to lining up time frames and historic price action with current price action. However, it takes a long time to get your brain to work against what it sees on the hard right edge of the screen. Books tell you wait for confirmation, I say active pro money is confirmation, and pro money is its own confirmation.

Hotochin,

Nice charting, all well done and roughing it out on the higher time frames is ok, we dont look for precise scientific areas or something that can be measured to the nth degree.

Your comment on the arrows is close. What they show is that each time pushes higher, the source of the bullish orders is checked to see will it hold, of so filter on more orders because that small pullback is enough to get many day traders stopped out. Its a low cost entry. You can stair step those entries all the way up into old supply. But of course you need the capital to do it and the patience to wait for them. My old charts show some of my scaled entries where I take up most of the origin of the move with my entry lines:)

The origin of the move was tested when price came back and sat on top of the blue box and then bolted out of there. That was classic pro money false move and load up the boat. Note the test they took and where it was. Some of those test work out to point perfection. Who would ever have thought?....there, I had to work in my old copyrighted line as I havent used it in an age.

Keep in mind that when price wants to turn at the end of the move, it will react to old areas of price action. When ever there are deeper pull backs be very wary, if price can hit one during a turn there is unlikely to be any orders worthy enough of keeping the trend in tact and the market can turn very fast and move a long way. If there are no buyers and all historic bullish orders are taken and we are at old supply on a major time frame i.e 4hr and higher, watch out below.

The price range on 1hr+ time frames makes it hard for more traders to see clearly, this is why you must mark those area right down to the 5min with a box and look for price action inside the box. The deeper price works into the box the more I get interested to trade against it especially when 4hr + is with us.

All make sense?

When you get used to trading this way, wait for the 5min to pull away from the extreme edge of the box, then come back to test the origin of that break, once that retest is done and both market timing for a major market is not near close or news to effect the pair is not due, then I will get in. Again as you progress you will find it hard to trade against the market, this is the counter intuitive part messing with your head. If it helps and lets assume you want to trade a 3 euro trade....instead put in a 1 euro trade, wait for the price to move and form another pull back which now is a retest of the previous break, now add in another 1 euro trade. For my US friends your Dollar is still worth something, just.....keep the presses going Ben:)

Rather than take the full risk on one trade, spread your risk over a few smaller size lots. When you improve you can then determine yourself which entries you are good at and take those heavier.

I will trade in places that contradict what I say in here, but I assure you my trades are only taken with a good many years at this and you will get a feel for when a decision point or a sudden spike becomes a viable trade. For the moment stick to what you are doing, it looks to me you are doing great at this and you have no problems on the higher time frames and have a good grasp now of the pull back setups too.

My old charts show some of my scaled entries where I take up most of the origin of the move with my entry lines:)

The origin of the move was tested when price came back and sat on top of the blue box and then bolted out of there. That was classic pro money false move and load up the boat. Note the test they took and where it was. Some of those test work out to point perfection. Who would ever have thought?....there, I had to work in my old copyrighted line as I havent used it in an age.

Keep in mind that when price wants to turn at the end of the move, it will react to old areas of price action. When ever there are deeper pull backs be very wary, if price can hit one during a turn there is unlikely to be any orders worthy enough of keeping the trend in tact and the market can turn very fast and move a long way. If there are no buyers and all historic bullish orders are taken and we are at old supply on a major time frame i.e 4hr and higher, watch out below.

The price range on 1hr+ time frames makes it hard for more traders to see clearly, this is why you must mark those area right down to the 5min with a box and look for price action inside the box. Doctor wrote: Hotochin,

Waiting for price to hit supply or demand on the monthly and weekly is not something you or I can afford. But we must be aware than when it does hit these areas there is going to be a reaction and a likely change in direction. Once the new direction has been decided by pro money, we now drop down into daily and lower time frames to look for pull backs counter to the decided direction and look for those pull backs to be the restest of the origin of the move. The retest appears deeper on lower time frames whereas the daily generally will not pull back very much.

If you think about it logically, any low time frame within a day traders pocket is ripe for false moves and stop hunts. This is how most of the larger orders get filled. When you see the price turn against a break of even a few hours, think of this as the test of the strength of the bulls or bears. If they want to continue with the move they will close some of the positions because you are now taking the orders as the market is moving. The false sense of security plays out on all low time frames and all it does is hand a very low cost and low risk entry for pro money to reverse price back on the direction of the chosen direction.

When price is between lets say the 4hr or higher time frame supply and demand, my choice is only take a trade once a pull back has come and it is into an area where pro money was active. If the move fails my risk is small. Ideally you should not take a trade when mid range between supply and demand and take the easy trades, the type you can see from across the room!

As you get more screen under your belt you will see how price wants to come back to the origin of the move. It will give you one and sometimes a second shot at getting in. There are a few gotchas in day trading and what can mess up nice entries just waiting to be taken are the release of news and the time of day. When London in particular opens and closes price will not always react as you expect if it is approaching an area of historic price action and its best to stand aside and wait for the market to settle.

It boils down to lining up time frames and historic price action with current price action. However, it takes a long time to get your brain to work against what it sees on the hard right edge of the screen. Books tell you wait for confirmation, I say active pro money is confirmation, and pro money is its own confirmation.

اگر منطقی فکر کنی، هر تایم‌فریم پایینی که در دسترس معامله‌گر روزانه است، آماده حرکت‌های فیک و شکار حد ضرر است. بیشتر سفارش‌های بزرگ همین‌طور پر می‌شوند. وقتی می‌بینی قیمت حتی بعد از شکستی که چند ساعت پیش رخ داده برمی‌گردد، این را آزمون قدرت صعودی‌ها یا خرس‌ها بدان. اگر بخواهند حرکت را ادامه بدهند، بخشی از پوزیشن‌ها را می‌بندند، چون تو الان داری سفارش‌ها را در حین حرکت بازار برمی‌داری. این حس امنیت کاذب در همه تایم‌فریم‌های پایین تکرار می‌شود و کارش فقط این است که یک ورود بسیار کم‌هزینه و کم‌ریسک به پول حرفه‌ای بدهد تا قیمت را در جهتِ انتخاب‌شده برگرداند.

وقتی قیمت بین عرضه و تقاضای مثلاً 4 ساعته یا بالاتر است، انتخاب من این است که فقط بعد از آمدن پولبک معامله بگیرم، آن هم وقتی پولبک به ناحیه‌ای رسیده که پول حرفه‌ای در آن فعال بوده. اگر حرکت شکست بخورد، ریسکم کم است. در حالت ایده‌آل نباید وقتی قیمت وسط محدوده بین عرضه و تقاضاست معامله بگیری؛ باید معامله‌های راحت را بگیری، از آن نوعی که از آن سر اتاق هم می‌بینی!

هرچه بیشتر پای چارت بنشینی می‌بینی قیمت چطور می‌خواهد به مبدأ حرکت برگردد. یک فرصت و گاهی فرصت دوم برای ورود به تو می‌دهد. در معامله روزانه چند دام هست و چیزهایی که می‌توانند ورودهای خوبِ آماده را خراب کنند، انتشار اخبار و ساعت روز است. مخصوصاً وقتی لندن باز و بسته می‌شود، اگر قیمت به ناحیه‌ای از پرایس اکشن تاریخی نزدیک شده باشد، همیشه آن‌طور که انتظار داری واکنش نشان نمی‌دهد و بهتر است کنار بایستی و صبر کنی بازار آرام شود.

خلاصه‌اش این است که تایم‌فریم‌ها و پرایس اکشن تاریخی را با پرایس اکشن فعلی هم‌راستا کنی. اما طول می‌کشد تا مغزت برخلاف آنچه در لبه راست چارت می‌بیند کار کند. کتاب‌ها می‌گویند منتظر تأیید بمان؛ من می‌گویم پول حرفه‌ایِ فعال خودش تأیید است، و پول حرفه‌ای تأیید خودش است.

Hotochin,

Not compression, if price moves from one area and relatively smoothly back to the candle that formed as the effect of the move then this is a pull back. Compression is more chaotic and candle an over lap and engulf each other in a very tight manner. Picture what you want to see as a stair step up in a bullish market, and inverse on the way down. When I get time to mark up a chart I will post one to show you. The place you marked compressed is correct but it was not what I was explaining yesterday. The pull backs is where the winning trades come from, compression is where you stay out and wait.

Compression is also price being of little interest to pro money and it wanders in the direction of the last historic area where pro money was active. The explosive move later which catches most by surprise. Unless there is a rapid retest on the 5min it may not be possible to trade those moves, you have to be watching it unfold and have the boxes drawn on your chart and see price react as it touches and enters the box. One single candle can be all it takes to retest and shoot out.

Look again at your last chart with the blue box.

Price returned to the top of the box and this was a test of the origin. Remember we are looking for it to penetrate deep as we can, but any touch of the box is what we. Where you take the trade is personal preference and based on risk and capital. Redraw the box again, but this time as the prlce where it had sat on top. Now you will see price came back here too, another buy, but with fewer bullish orders remaining.

maknil,

I dont have a natural gas chart to see the remaining time frames, but from what you posted you bought near the top. If you are trading lower time frames and for lower point profit it may work out. posts.t:
Ok guys here is a chart to help explain pro money tests and what books call trend. But their idea of trend is long after the origin of the move which is why supply/demand trading creates more profit.

The bottom of the chart shows a box which is demand. Price pushes through the box, comes back to test it and moves away cleanly after. This shows pro bulls in control. If the test of this demand was something you didnt catch, you can wait until you see a less dramatic move. There are numerous white horizontal lines on the chart and these show price pushing above the last created high and these are the pull backs I refer to. These are areas where pro money will either close positions, adjust by adding more and a combination of both. Note how price tests even the break of these small areas. This happens on many time frames and when the market is moving this is one sign you must be aware of.

As previously mentioned we are not looking for pixel perfect tests, although it can be alarmingly accurate at times, we want to see these tests as shake outs of the weak hands, those wont went long on the break only to see price come back and stop them out. Part of the reason is far too many traders place stops where pro money know where to look. Books tell you place a stop below a swing or below the last bullish candle and so on. Now that you know where to look and can train your brain where stops will be and where pro money is likely to enter, you have a valuable tool by which to pull nice money from the market.

What I described is ideal for people beginning and as you gain more confidence you can look to try out scaling in and out at the beginning and end of these overall moves where a higher time frame provides the intel for the areas to draw the boxes for supply and demand.

I hope this is useful and it gels in your head and becomes second nature.

The point behind the chart is the show the principle and not pixel perfect detail. On a lower time frame you will see some pull backs even though none will be very deep or to the break of the move up. If you are thinking ahead of my chart then you are on the right track. When a lower time frame presents an opportunity you can take it as a day trader. My chart is a daily and few of us will wait around for that to unwind before getting in.

If you examine the same pair on a lower time frame and with a zoomed out view there will be many long entries there. In the past I spoke of cycles or phases and thats the wind shown there and will be represented as a fractal of other time frames. What looks like a pull back in a higher time frame is a shorting opportunity on a lower time frame once you close the position before higher time frame demand. This is counter trend but works once you know what you are doing and crystal clear about the reaction areas.

You can see how the pull backs will last up into the final push and then there is higher time reaction to be concerned about. I am out before that reaction and bag what points I can.

I am glad it helps clear up the text, visual aids help a lot.

Those who latched onto my S&P500 comments recently should be making nice money today. And it may provide nice entries as it falls and a good demonstration of bearish entries. If not in already, just watch it for now.

Hotochin,

1. I used usd/jpy only because the price action was nice and it fitted on one chart with crystal clear movement. The white horizontal lines are where more bullish entries are placed. As price pushed up in another move, it will turn back down and test the most recent push. Once this is tested, I enter long. I am satisfied to continue placing entries until I am fully committed to the amount of capital I wish to invest and the cost in risk. The target for me will be a higher time frame area. But day traders may be happy with a set point profit i.e x points or just watch it until it turns and then close out. There are a hundred ways to trade a move.

2. The only logical way to trade is once we have a new month, do you analysis on the monthly chart, then the weekly and the daily. On each new week where there is no new monthly close, work from the weekly down, then on each new day where there is no new weekly candle close, work from the daily down. You must be 100% aware of where all time frames are ALL THE TIME.

Once you have that intel you are better positioned to look for lower time frame entries.

Once a higher time frame hits historic supply or demand I wait for price to react and give me the new direction, or continuation. This is where those white lines after a reaction come in, if the trade off the first test was missed. If you want earlier entries you will need wide stops because you know from experience pro money wont give you an easy time or a simple trade. If the heat is too much, wait for a later entry where the direction is obvious and then take a pull back entry where a test is clear in your mind. How long you wait i,e the time frame is totally your decision and I cant tell you which to take. I will take any of them and if price action and tests are not very clear I can stay out or scale in. Like I say, its down to the risk you wish to take.

I hear it all the time from traders who place a trade see it go in their direction and suddenly price comes back against them, stop them out, and price reverse back in the direction of the original move. This is what I mentioned earlier with stop hunting and pro money getting cheaper prices to filter more orders in. This never changes and has been like this since the markets began. The lesson is do not take break outs, wait for a pull back and then enter once there is room for profit in the eyes of pro money, and that is a nice distance from the next supply or demand area.

3. I wouldnt call it play money, those guys make enough in a week to buy a small country. A spike on a 4hr chart is worth billions. A 24hr day is worth 4 trillion. That is not play money and they dont get it use it unless they know what they are doing. Contrary to your other comment about pro money getting efficient pricing, they have always gotten better entry prices than we do. They are the market movers, we ride on their coat tails at a more costly entry. We cannot move the market, we do not have the capital to do so. The latent flow is what happens in the pull backs I keep mentioning. It is no more exciting than left over orders that sit there wait to be filled. Some are automated orders and some are manual. The HF stuff comes in there too.

Price goes between supply and demand on ever increasing time frames, as it works it way it will go up and down as orders are filled, closed and adjusted. There is nothing secret about how it works, in fact I find it all rather boring.

وقتی تایم‌فریم بالاتر به عرضه یا تقاضای تاریخی می‌رسد، صبر می‌کنم قیمت واکنش نشان دهد و جهت جدید یا ادامه حرکت را به من بدهد. اینجا همان خطوط سفیدی است که بعد از یک واکنش می‌آید، اگر معامله از آزمون اول را از دست داده باشی. اگر ورودهای زودتر می‌خواهی، به استاپ‌های بازتر نیاز داری، چون از تجربه می‌دانی پول حرفه‌ای کار را برایت راحت نمی‌کند و معامله ساده‌ای نمی‌دهد. اگر فشار زیاد است، صبر کن برای ورود دیرتر که جهت واضح است و بعد یک ورود روی پولبک بگیر که آزمونش برایت روشن است. اینکه چقدر صبر کنی، یعنی همان تایم‌فریم، کاملاً تصمیم خودت است و نمی‌توانم بگویم کدام را انتخاب کن. من هر کدامشان را می‌گیرم و اگر پرایس اکشن و آزمون‌ها خیلی واضح نباشد، می‌توانم بیرون بمانم یا پله‌ای وارد شوم. همان‌طور که گفتم، به ریسکی بستگی دارد که می‌خواهی بپذیری.

مدام از معامله‌گرهایی می‌شنوم که معامله‌ای می‌گیرند، می‌بینند در جهتشان می‌رود و ناگهان قیمت برمی‌گردد و استاپشان می‌زند و بعد قیمت دوباره در جهت حرکت اولیه برمی‌گردد. این همان چیزی است که قبلاً درباره شکار حد ضرر و گرفتن قیمت‌های ارزان‌تر توسط پول حرفه‌ای برای فیلتر کردن سفارش‌های بیشتر گفتم. این هرگز تغییر نمی‌کند و از وقتی بازارها شروع شده‌اند همین‌طور بوده. درسش این است: سراغ شکست‌ها نرو، صبر کن برای پولبک و بعد وارد شو، وقتی از دید پول حرفه‌ای فضای سود وجود دارد؛ و آن فاصله خوبی از ناحیه عرضه یا تقاضای بعدی است.

3. من اسمش را پول بازی نمی‌گذارم؛ این جماعت در یک هفته آن‌قدر درمی‌آورند که یک کشور کوچک بخرند. یک اسپایک روی چارت 4 ساعته میلیاردها می‌ارزد. یک روز 24 ساعته 4 تریلیون می‌ارزد. این پول بازی نیست و آن را به دست نمی‌آورند و خرج نمی‌کنند مگر بدانند چه می‌کنند. برخلاف آن حرف دیگرت درباره اینکه پول حرفه‌ای قیمت‌گذاری کارآمد می‌گیرد، آن‌ها همیشه قیمت ورود بهتری از ما گرفته‌اند. آن‌ها بازار را حرکت می‌دهند و ما با ورود گران‌تر، از دم‌شان آویزان می‌شویم. ما نمی‌توانیم بازار را حرکت بدهیم، سرمایه‌اش را نداریم. جریان نهفته همان چیزی است که در پولبک‌هایی که مدام از آن حرف می‌زنم رخ می‌دهد. هیچ هیجان بیشتری از سفارش‌های باقی‌مانده‌ای که آنجا نشسته‌اند و منتظر پر شدن‌اند ندارد. بعضی سفارش‌ها خودکارند و بعضی دستی. چیزهای فرکانس بالا هم آنجا سر و کله‌شان پیدا می‌شود.

قیمت بین عرضه و تقاضا در تایم‌فریم‌های هرچه بزرگ‌تر حرکت می‌کند؛ همان‌طور که راهش را می‌رود، بالا و پایین می‌رود چون سفارش‌ها پر، بسته و تنظیم می‌شوند. در اینکه چطور کار می‌کند هیچ رازی نیست؛ در واقع من همه‌اش را نسبتاً خسته‌کننده می‌دانم.
